conditions: short of full out nuclear war

statement.excerpt: Nothing China can realistically do (short of full out nuclear war) is going to stop companies like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon from serving generative AI on the cloud.
statement.document_title: The core misconception that is driving American AI policy

from_speaker: short of full out nuclear war
serving generative AI on the cloud
our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns preventing major US providers from operating their cloud generative AI businesses, including serving US customers.
A Chinese regional ban, retirement of one model, or temporary outage does not establish that a provider has been stopped from serving cloud generative AI.
An actual Chinese action would demonstrate feasibility; reliable evidence must also establish that it caused the cessation.
The nuclear-war exception limits qualifying causes. It is not an antecedent that must occur before the forecast can be evaluated.
criteria.support_condition: The named providers remain able to supply cloud generative AI despite Chinese actions throughout the unlimited horizon. Finite continued operation cannot prove this universal prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A realistically executed Chinese action other than full nuclear war causes a named or comparable major US provider to cease its cloud generative AI business, rather than merely restricting one region or product.

evidence.explanation: AWS documented an operational feature for hosted generative models. Continuing service does not prove that no future Chinese action could stop it.
Microsoft's September recap describes Azure-hosted Claude availability. It supplies evidence of continued service, not an assessment of all possible Chinese interventions.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verified business-wide cessation at a named or comparable major US provider, causally attributable to Chinese action other than full nuclear war, would contradict the forecast.
